summary: OpenAI published a builder's guide describing new Responses API primitives (programmatic tool calling, native multi-agent orchestration, persisted reasoning/compaction, extended prompt caching) for GPT-5.6, illustrating cost and performance gains reported by startups.

mechanisms.reason: The document reports a benchmark score held roughly constant while cost per run fell by roughly 25x between model generations, indicating a genuine drop in compute/work per token rather than just a price cut.
mechanisms.quote: Three months ago, GPT‑5.5 (Extra High) scored 84.36% on this benchmark for a total cost of $33.27. At launch, GPT‑5.6 Luna (Extra High) delivers essentially the same performance, scoring 84.04% at a cost of $1.33.

mechanisms.reason: OpenAI describes a native multi-agent orchestration capability built into the API that coordinates multiple agents across parallel workstreams, and states it is also how ChatGPT's ultra capability setting works, indicating scale beyond a single customer's architecture.
mechanisms.quote: Parallel decomposition where appropriate: using native multi-agent orchestration allows coordinating multiple agents across parallel workstreams to finish complex tasks faster.

practices.reason: GPT-5.6's smaller models retain most of the prior flagship's accuracy at a small fraction of the cost, changing which model tier a team should default to for agentic and extraction workloads.
practices.quote: Luna keeps 98% of GPT‑5.5’s extraction accuracy at one-eighteenth the cost.

practices.reason: Programmatic Tool Calling and native multi-agent orchestration are concrete, implementable API patterns with stated token and quality gains that an engineering team could build agent pipelines around.
practices.quote: In our evaluations, GPT‑5.6 using Programmatic Tool Calling matched our rubric quality while using 21% fewer input tokens.

practices.reason: Extended prompt cache TTL and deterministic cache breakpoints are directly usable API controls that reduce uncached input and improve cache hit rates for any team serving on this API.
practices.quote: the prompt cache TTL has been extended to a minimum of 30 minutes and cache breakpoints can now be set deterministically within a model’s context window.

practices.reason: The ARC-AGI-3 harness result shows that retained reasoning and compaction alone (no model change) nearly tripled the score while using far fewer tokens, which changes what a team should measure and how it should configure eval harnesses.
practices.quote: on ARC-AGI-3, GPT‑5.6 Sol scored 13.3% with the standard harness. After enabling retained reasoning and compaction, however, the score jumped to 38.3%—while using roughly 6× fewer output tokens.

notable_reason: The document discloses a roughly 25x reduction in cost for equivalent benchmark performance between consecutive model generations, a magnitude of efficiency gain that materially resets expectations for inference economics.
